summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with poorly controlled type II diabetes and a history of diabetic retinopathy, was admitted with shortness of breath and a productive cough. She was found to have multifocal pneumonia on chest X-ray, involving the left lower and right upper lobes, and was treated with intravenous then oral levofloxacin. She also presented with metabolic acidosis and hyperglycemia, which improved with IV fluids and insulin therapy. Metformin was held during admission due to acidosis risk but was restarted before discharge. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home on a continued insulin regimen, metformin, lisinopril, and a three-day course of oral levofloxacin. Follow-up was advised for a repeat chest X-ray in six weeks and primary care evaluation of her diabetes control.
problems: Diabetes with ophthalmic manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
